extracted.intended_audience: NIH/PHS grant applicants and institutional grant administrators (PD/PIs, Signing Officials, Administrative Officials, SOs/AOs, and application initiators) who will prepare and submit applications using ASSIST
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guidance for preparing, validating, finalizing, submitting, and tracking NIH and other PHS grant applications using the ASSIST web system, covering both single-project and multi-project workflows and related access/role rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find a Funding Opportunity and record the Notice Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a Funding Opportunity and record the Notice Number (e.g., PA-25-425).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Funding Opportunity notice number when initiating an application in ASSIST; this is the first step for both single-project and multi-project applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make a submission plan and gather eRA Commons usernames
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a submission plan. Decide who will be responsible for data entry in ASSIST and gather their eRA Commons usernames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan responsibilities (data entry, component leads) before beginning; collecting eRA Commons IDs up-front avoids delays when assigning roles and granting access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Login to ASSIST with eRA Commons credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Login to ASSIST using your eRA Commons username and password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All ASSIST actions (initiate, edit, validate, submit) require an eRA Commons login; some actions require specific roles (e.g., SO role for submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate the application using the Initiate Application feature and Notice Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Initiate Application feature and your Notice Number to get started on your application. Or, access applications already in progress using the Search feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiating with the correct notice number ensures the right forms and FOA-specific instructions are loaded; Search lets you continue work already started.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide and manage application access to team members
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide application access to your team. Automatic Edit access is given to all SOs and AOs at the applicant organization, the PD/PIs designated on the application (once eRA Commons username is entered), and the user that initiated the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Manage Access action to give or revoke access to additional users. Ensure PD/PIs' eRA Commons credentials are entered so they gain edit access. Be mindful of who can edit forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete required forms in the correct order (R&R Cover first)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the tabs across the top of the screen to move between forms. Complete the R&R Cover tab first. Add Optional Forms as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the recommended form order (R&R Cover first) to ensure correct assembly; add optional forms only if the FOA or application requires them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate multi-user editing constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple users can simultaneously work on your application, but only one user at a time can Edit an individual form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan concurrent work to avoid conflicts; if someone has a form open for edit, others can view but not edit that same form until it is released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate application data against NIH business rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Validate Application action to check your entered data against NIH business rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run validation frequently to catch errors early. For multi-project applications, use Validate Component as well as Validate Application to check component-level issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preview application image and check for assembly issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Preview Application action to generate a draft application image in the agency format. Check the application image for any assembly issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully inspect the assembled e-Application image (PDF) to ensure forms and attachments appear correctly; check associated documents in the Other Relevant Documents div of the screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalize status before submission (Update Submission/Component Status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Update Submission Status action to change your application from Work In Progress status to Ready for Submission status. For multi-project applications, use Update Component Status and Update Submission Status actions to lock down editing and prepare your application for submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional edits are needed after locking, return the application/component to Work In Progress. Locking is necessary to prevent further edits before final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit through ASSIST with appropriate SO role and Grants.gov AOR credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Submit button on the Summary tab to submit to the agency through Grants.gov. The Submit button is only active for users logged into ASSIST with an eRA Commons account with the SO role. Provide your valid Grants.gov Authorized Organizational Representative username and password when prompted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure someone with the SO role and the organization's Grants.gov AOR credentials is available at submission time. Without the SO role or AOR credentials the Submit action will not complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track application status and verify Agency Tracking Number and eRA Commons processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the View Submission Status Details link to track your application status. If your application successfully processed through to eRA Commons, the 7-digit Agency Tracking # will be hyperlinked to the eRA Commons detailed status screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the linked Agency Tracking # to confirm processing; monitor status for errors or rejections returned from Grants.gov or eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carefully check assembled application image and Other Relevant Documents after processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully check your assembled application image (e-Application) and associated documents in the Other Relevant Documents div of the screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm all attachments, signatures, and forms are present and correctly assembled after eRA Commons processing; catching assembly issues post-processing allows timely corrections if allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project: understand FOA component rules and define layout and leads
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully read the Funding Opportunity, noting allowable types of required/optional components and any special instructions. Understand the structure of NIH multi-project applications and how Multi-project Application Images are assembled. Define the layout of your application (e.g., define components and who will lead each).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FOAs often have FOA-specific component requirements and special instructions for multi-project (e.g., required cores, research project components). Define component leads and responsibilities early to coordinate data entry and validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project: use Add New Component and component navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Add New Component action to build out your application. Use the left-hand component navigation and the top form tabs to move between components and forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build and organize components consistently; complete each component's R&R Cover and required forms. Component-level navigation helps manage complex multi-project applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available ASSIST resources and guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult ASSIST Quick Start Guides, ASSIST User Guide, ASSIST Presentations, videos, and related links (ASSIST Log In, Application Instructions, Annotated Form Sets, ASSIST Online Help).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these resources for detailed walkthroughs, examples (annotated sample PDFs), and troubleshooting. The page lists Quick Start Guides (single- and multi-project), User Guide (PDF), and presentations for specific application types (e.g., small business).
